name: Tannuk, Steadfast Second
oracle_text:
Other creatures you control have haste.
Artifact cards and red creature cards in your hand have warp {2}{R}. (You may cast a card from your hand for its warp cost. Exile that permanent at the beginning of the next end step, then you may cast it from exile on a later turn.)
blocked_sentences: Artifact cards and red creature cards in your hand have warp {2}{R}. (You may cast a card from your hand for its warp cost. Exile that permanent at the beginning of the next end step, then you may cast it from exile on a later turn.)

needs.what: `warp` as a card-level cost key beside `evoke`, `foretell` and `suspend`: a mana string naming an alternative cost payable while casting the card from hand, plus the two riders the rule bolts on and which are the whole point of the mechanic. (1) A flag on the resulting permanent recording that the warp cost was paid -- the same shape `evoke` already keeps and `condition_keys` already reads as `evoked` -- since only a warped permanent is exiled. (2) A delayed trigger created on resolution, at the beginning of the next end step, exiling that permanent; it must be the engine's own, not written on the card, because the card printing "Warp {1}{R}" prints no such ability and the residual gate would find no line for it. (3) A standing permission on the exiled card to be cast from exile on a later turn for its printed cost -- `playable_duration: "later_turns"` already exists in `playable_durations` and is the right span, but nothing currently attaches it as part of a cost being paid. Being a card-level cost rather than an ability matters for the usual reason: a card in hand has no abilities, and warp is offered while the card is still in hand.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `card_level_cost_keys` carries 25 prices and none of them is this shape. `evoke` is the closest and stops halfway: it is an unconditional alternative mana cost from hand with a readable `evoked` flag, which is exactly warp's first half, but evoke buys a sacrifice written on the card's own trigger, and a warped permanent's exile is supplied by the rule and is never printed -- writing it as a `delayed_trigger` ability on every warp card leaves a `text` with no printed sentence to claim, which is a gate rejection. `foretell` and `suspend` are the nearest shipped shapes for the exile half and are the wrong way round: both exile from HAND first and cast the card later out of exile, whereas warp casts first and exiles the permanent afterwards, so the card spends a turn on the battlefield that foretell never gives it. `madness` likewise exiles in place of a discard. `rebound` is the only rider that casts something again on a later turn and it is exclusive to instants and sorceries cast from hand, exiling the SPELL as it resolves and casting it again on your very next upkeep -- not a permanent exiled at end step and cast at the caster's leisure on any later turn. `exiles_itself` is a one-way trip with no permission to return, and `grant_playable` / `exile`'s `playable_this_turn` grant a permission from a resolving effect, not from a cost somebody paid.

needs.what: A static effect that hands a card-level cost to OTHER cards in a hand -- `grant_warp` (or a general `grant_card_cost`) whose `affects` is a `static_filter_keys` filter over cards in your hand and whose payload is a warp cost, here `{2}{R}`. The filter this card needs is a union of two printed shapes, `{"types": ["Artifact"]}` and `{"types": ["Creature"], "colors": ["R"]}`, both printed characteristics, so it is within what a static may lawfully read; but it must be evaluated on cards in the HAND zone, and the granted cost must then be offered by the casting code as though the card had printed it.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Every entry in `card_level_cost_keys` is a field on the card that prints the word -- the schema puts `evoke`, `foretell`, `suspend` and the rest on the card model itself -- and no static in `static_effects` can put one on a different card. `grant_keyword` is the obvious candidate and cannot reach it twice over: the loader knows only the 34 ability keywords in `keywords` and warp is not among them, and warp is a price rather than an ability keyword, so it would be the wrong mechanism even if the word existed. `grant_ability` hands over a triggered, activated or static ability, and a cost is none of the three; a granted activated ability also works on the battlefield only, while this grant must be live on cards sitting in hand. `spell_cost_reduction` and `ability_cost_reduction` are the only statics that touch what a spell costs and they only discount the printed cost -- they cannot offer a second, separate cost, and a {2}{R} reduction is a different card that would misprice every artifact in hand. `cast_as_though_flash` and `cast_from_graveyard` show that statics can change HOW and WHENCE other cards are cast, so the hook exists; none of them changes WHAT IS PAID. `grant_playable` is a resolving op leaving a permission on specific objects at their printed price, not a standing static over a changing hand.

notes: The other printed line is expressible and was checked against the vocabulary before filing: "Other creatures you control have haste." is a static `grant_keyword` with `keywords: ["haste"]` and `affects: {"types": ["Creature"], "controller": "you", "exclude_self": true}` -- `haste` is in `keywords`, and `exclude_self` is in `static_filter_keys`. So this card is one mechanic away from finished, and once warp exists it has a real gate-5 assertion available: `battlefield_count` 33 and `granted` `{"keywords": ["haste"], "count": 2}` for the position's two other creatures.
